name: NY-22
label: Safe D

key_factors: Markets price Mannion at ~94% to win
Mannion has a 10-to-1 fundraising advantage and $1.8M on hand
District leans Democratic by 4 points with a favorable environment
No polls or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Mannion: a Democratic-leaning seat, incumbency, a favorable national environment, and a dominant cash advantage over Buller, who has raised under $300K. Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price his win odds around 94%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Buller closing within single digits would warrant a downgrade to Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent John Mannion defends a central New York seat that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $2.7 million and holding $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups have spent against Mannion so far.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the picture rests on fundamentals and markets. Betting markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both give Mannion roughly 94 percent odds, and the favorable national environment adds to his advantage. The race remains Safe Democratic, though the lack of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat wider than usual.
